text:
Logan Cooley is playing like the best player on a good team, which is what the Coyotes drafted him third overall to become. He has 25 points in 21 games, 16 of them on the power play, and 14 in his last ten, with his ice time up two minutes a night since Nick Schmaltz went down. The best part for Utah is that the hot stretch is earned: he is getting more chances, 4.5 expected goals on his own shots over those ten games against 3.5 usual (expected goals measure the quality of chances), and Utah takes 59% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on.

The part that won't last is the shooting. He has 12 goals on 6.8 expected, a 34% rate, and nobody keeps that up. Our range still has him around 83 points by April. Watch him at the offensive blue line: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries. Colorado learned this week that Utah takes care of him; Gabriel Landeskog was fined for cross-checking him, and Jack McBain fought Landeskog for it.
